extracted.intended_audience: researchers preparing NIH grant biographical sketches (PIs, co-investigators, senior key personnel)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing the NIH-formatted biographical sketch for an NIH grant application, including required sections (Personal Statement, Positions and Honors, Contributions to Science, Research Support) and meeting page/format constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limit / length
rubrics_metrics.description: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entire biosketch must fit within five pages. Keep each section concise and prioritize the most relevant information for the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education/Training content and format
rubrics_metrics.description: EDUCATION/TRAINING (Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, include postdoctoral training and residency training if applicable. Add/delete rows as necessary.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List institution and location, degree (if applicable), completion date (MM/YYYY), and field of study. Begin with undergraduate (baccalaureate) and include graduate, residency, and postdoctoral training; add or delete rows to fit the individual's history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A. Personal Statement (narrative of relevant background, experience, and role on the project).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize your research focus and relevant experience, describe specific prior collaborations and publications relevant to the proposed work, and state the role you will play on this application (e.g., 'I will serve as the primary biostatistician' or 'I will serve as co-investigator'). Use this section to justify your contribution to the project and highlight specific expertise or leadership that supports your proposed role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positions and Employment / Professional Memberships and Service
rubrics_metrics.description: B. Positions and Honors / Service and Professional memberships (chronological list of positions, dates, and professional service).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a chronological list of positions and employment with dates (years), including institutional affiliations and titles. Also list significant service roles, committee memberships, leadership positions (e.g., Chair, Scientific Chair), and professional memberships. Include honors and awards in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributions to Science
rubrics_metrics.description: C. Contributions to Science (narrative descriptions of major scientific contributions with representative publications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe key contributions to the field in a short narrative for each topical area. For each contribution, explain its significance/impact and provide representative citations (numbered). Use sub-items (a., b., c., etc.) for representative publications. Emphasize how the work advanced understanding, influenced guidelines, or led to practical changes in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Support (Ongoing and Past)
rubrics_metrics.description: D. Research Support (selected) — list ongoing and past research support with role and dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List grant number, funding agency, project title, overall goal/aims in one sentence, role on the project (e.g., Principal Investigator, Co-Investigator), and the project start and end dates. Separate Ongoing and Past support and include brief descriptions of the project's aims and relevance to the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide complete publication list reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete list of published work (>250 publications): http://... (example shown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, provide a URL or reference to a complete list of published work (e.g., PubMed/My NCBI bibliography) for readers who want the full publication record beyond representative citations in Contributions to Science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of representative published citations in sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative publications are cited with full reference information and PMIDs/PMCIDs where available (used in Personal Statement and Contributions to Science).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full citation details for representative works (authors, title, journal, date, volume(issue):pages) and include PMID/PMCID when available to permit easy verification and to demonstrate relevance and productivity. Number representative citations for cross-reference in narratives.
